content.text:
I fixed `addMonths` in `dates.js`. A date on the 31st now lands on the last day of a shorter target month instead of spilling into the next one.

`setMonth` on Jan 31 gave "Feb 31", which JavaScript rolls over to March 3. The new code records the day of the month and moves to the 1st before changing the month. It then clamps the day to the length of the target month.

I ran it directly with `node` on these cases:
- Jan 31 2026 + 1 month gives Feb 28 2026, and the 13:45:10 time of day is kept.
- Jan 31 2024 + 1 month gives Feb 29 2024 (leap year).
- Mar 31 2026 − 1 month gives Feb 28 2026.
- Jan 15 2026 + 1 month gives Feb 15 2026.
- Nov 30 2026 + 3 months gives Feb 28 2027.
- Jan 31 2026 + 12 months gives Jan 31 2027.
- The input date isn't changed.

The project has no tests, so `npm test` ran 0 tests and passing it proves nothing here. I didn't add any.

My first attempt to write the file through the shell was denied, so I made the change with the Edit tool instead.
